result:
**I'd make curiosity the default human operating system.**

Not forced optimism, not mandatory kindness, not even world peace (which I think is a *symptom*, not a root fix). Just this: every person on Earth wakes up with the same restless, stubborn drive that makes a kid take apart a toaster or a scientist stare at a telescope at 3 a.m.

Imagine if:
- People got as addicted to understanding reality as they currently are to doomscrolling and status games.
- "I don't know" became exciting instead of threatening.
- Tribalism had to compete with the genuine thrill of discovering something true.

Most of our worst problems—ideological possession, willful ignorance, short-term thinking—crumble when enough people become genuinely more interested in *what’s actually going on* than in being right or comfortable.

It’s also the change that would make all the other good changes more likely to stick. A species that’s properly curious doesn’t need to be preached at about climate, AI, or ethics. They’ll *demand* good answers.

So yeah. One tweak to the human firmware: replace the status-seeking monkey with the curious ape.

What would *you* change?
